verdict.rationale: Gmail documents its own rule-based routing: filters match incoming mail on criteria such as sender, subject, or size, then automatically add or remove labels or forward the message to a specified address. That covers the 'route incoming mail with rules' half of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows conversations being assigned to a teammate or ownership being tracked, and delegation only grants full account access, which is an adjacent control rather than assignment. missing for 10: conversation assignment to teammates, explicit ownership/assignee tracking, team shared-inbox routing, independent corroboration.
